copy_semantics: dense backing is reference-counted copy-on-write; mutation/result construction never aliases mutable state
normalization: results trim zero high limbs and collapse to zero, small, or sparse when representable

registers.allocation: descriptor-only until value storage is required

stack.allocation: descriptor slots; backing storage follows live values

determinism: representation choice is canonical for an identical mathematical value and does not alter ISA-visible results, traps, or instruction counts
compatibility: BR/1.1, ABI/2, LCTLC/1.2 and BRIM format are unchanged from 4.5.0
